sugar.description: sugar-sensing gustatory receptor neurons (right hemisphere), the 'give sugar' stimulus of the paper's example
sugar.source: Shiu et al. 2024 (Nature 634, 210-219), example.ipynb in github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model, commit 91bdd1e, MIT; ids come from FlyWire v630, 20 of 21 exist in v783

mn9.description: MN9, the motor neuron of the proboscis-extension muscle the paper reads out for sugar (labelled CB0701 in our annotations)
mn9.source: Shiu et al. 2024 (Nature 634, 210-219), example.ipynb in github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model, commit 91bdd1e, MIT (id_mn9)

bitter.description: bitter-sensing gustatory receptor neurons (labellar, right hemisphere) that Shiu et al. stimulate against sugar
bitter.source: Shiu et al. 2024 (Nature 634, 210-219), github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model commit 91bdd1e, MIT, figures.ipynb cell 23 (neu_bitter); ids come from FlyWire v630, 20 of 21 exist in v783

water.description: water-sensing gustatory receptor neurons (labellar, right hemisphere)
water.source: Shiu et al. 2024 (Nature 634, 210-219), github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model commit 91bdd1e, MIT, figures.ipynb cell 32 (neu_water); ids come from FlyWire v630, 18 of 18 exist in v783

jo_ce.description: Johnston's organ C/E neurons (antennal mechanosensory) that Shiu et al. map to antennal grooming
jo_ce.source: Shiu et al. 2024 (Nature 634, 210-219), github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model commit 91bdd1e, MIT, figures.ipynb cell 50 (neu_JON_CE); ids come from FlyWire v630, 69 of 70 exist in v783

abn1.description: aBN1, the brain neuron the paper reads out for antennal grooming
abn1.source: Shiu et al. 2024 (Nature 634, 210-219), github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model commit 91bdd1e, MIT, figures.ipynb cell 62 (id_aBN1)

dnp01.description: DNp01, the giant-fiber descending neurons of the escape pathway
dnp01.source: FlyWire annotations v783 (cell_type DNp01); descending giant fiber, escape pathway; readout works when driven directly, looming selectivity was not shown in this model

dng100.description: DNg100, the pair of descending neurons (one per side) whose activation is linked to walking; used here as a direct-activation (optogenetics-like) stimulus for the body
dng100.source: FlyWire annotations v783 (cell_type DNg100, side left and right); direct activation, NOT a sensory pathway: behavior link: DNg100 drives walking (Pugliese et al. 2026, Nature; Bidaye et al. 2020, Neuron, for the DN walking-command class); the brain model does not show which sensory input recruits it

dna02_left.description: DNa02 on the LEFT side (one neuron), a direct-activation (optogenetics-like) steering stimulus for the body
dna02_left.source: FlyWire annotations v783 (cell_type DNa02, side left); direct activation, NOT a sensory pathway: behavior link: DNa02 activity predicts ipsilateral steering (Rayshubskiy et al. 2025, eLife 102230)

dna02_right.description: DNa02 on the RIGHT side (one neuron), a direct-activation (optogenetics-like) steering stimulus for the body
dna02_right.source: FlyWire annotations v783 (cell_type DNa02, side right); direct activation, NOT a sensory pathway: behavior link: DNa02 activity predicts ipsilateral steering (Rayshubskiy et al. 2025, eLife 102230)
